title: Guerrilla Warfare: A Method
author: Che Guevara
context: Published in September 1963 in the theoretical journal Cuba Socialista, this seminal essay by Ernesto 'Che' Guevara synthesizes the military, political, and economic principles of the Cuban Revolution into a strategic method for continental anti-imperialist struggle in Latin America and the Global South. Guevara establishes that guerrilla warfare is a political weapon aimed at the conquest of state power, requiring the mobilization of the peasant masses and the creation of subjective revolutionary consciousness.
relatesToToday: Offers critical strategic lessons for modern asymmetric and popular struggles fighting deeply entrenched, heavily militarized state apparatuses and foreign-backed oligarchies.
keyTakeaways: Guerrilla warfare is not an end in itself, but a political instrument for the conquest of state power.
Subjective conditions of organization and leadership can be created and accelerated through armed mass struggle rather than waited for passively.
The national bourgeoisie of the dependent world is incapable of leading genuine anti-imperialist liberation due to fear of the working masses.
